[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Caching Strategies in Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Caching is a crucial technique for improving the performance and scalability of web applications. By storing the results of expensive database queries or heavy computations in memory, Flask can serve subsequent requests much faster."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Installation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To implement caching in a Flask application, the most popular extension used is Flask-Caching. You can install it using pip."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install Flask-Caching"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Flask-Caching"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once installed, you need to initialize the Cache extension in your application factory or main Flask application file. Here is how you can set up a simple in-memory cache."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask
from flask_caching import Cache

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config['CACHE_TYPE'] = 'SimpleCache'
app.config['CACHE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT'] = 300
cache = Cache(app)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Caching Route Responses"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The easiest way to cache data in Flask is by using the @cache.cached decorator on your route handlers. This caches the entire response for the specified timeout duration."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"@app.route('/expensive-data')
@cache.cached(timeout=60)
def get_expensive_data():
    # Simulate a heavy database query or external API call
    return {'data': 'This is expensive data'}"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Redis for Distributed Caching"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"For production environments where your Flask application runs on multiple workers or servers, an in-memory cache is not sufficient. You should use Redis as a centralized caching backend."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"app.config['CACHE_TYPE'] = 'RedisCache'
app.config['CACHE_REDIS_URL'] = 'redis://localhost:6379/0'
cache = Cache(app)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Caching"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set appropriate timeouts to prevent serving stale data to users for too long."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cache only data that is expensive to compute or fetch, and changes infrequently."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement cache invalidation strategies when underlying database records are updated or deleted."}]
